functionality.rationale: Terminal-state mistakes can either accept frames after a fatal error or incorrectly kill a healthy stream-scoped transcript.

security.rationale: Continuing after connection-fatal framing or negotiation errors processes attacker input after parser state is no longer trustworthy.

performance.rationale: The fix adds one terminal-state branch per transcript frame without changing allocation or framing limits.

compatibility.rationale: All valid transcripts and stream-scoped post-binding failures must retain their existing behavior.

concurrency.rationale: TranscriptParser remains a caller-confined mutable parser and gains no asynchronous or shared access.

platform.rationale: The state classification is platform-neutral C++ and must pass native builds on every desktop target.

persistence.rationale: The parser state is process-local and does not change any persisted schema or recovery format.

adr.rationale: The fix restores the connection-fatal rules already specified in protocol v1 section 14.

architecture.rationale: The implementation remains inside the canonical protocol target and changes no dependency boundary.

roadmap.rationale: This closes a parser defect without completing a new product milestone.

defect.symptom: TranscriptParser accepts a valid frame after returning a connection-fatal framing error.
defect.expected_contract: Protocol v1 section 14 requires malformed framing and negotiation failures to terminate the connection because shared parser state is no longer trustworthy.
defect.actual_behavior: A malformed frame returns MALFORMED_FRAME, but the same parser then accepts a valid message with the next unchanged message ID.
defect.trigger: Process a truncated declared frame, then process a valid initiator HELLO with message ID 1 on the same TranscriptParser.
